 After Karhutla, West Java DPRD asks for full alert and mountain slopes to be checked before the peak of the rainy season 
 31 Oktober 2026, 21:35 | Editorial Team 
 Tim VOI 
 Reporter 
 Advento C Saudale 
 Editor 
 BPBD officers help residents evacuate due to flooding submerging their homes in Tanjungsari Village, Tasikmalaya Regency, West Java, Thursday, March 9, 2023. (ANTARA/HO-BPBD Tasikmalaya Regency) 
 Share:
 BANDUNG - Deputy Chairman of the West Java DPRD Iwan Suryawan asked the West Java Provincial Government to immediately examine the strength of the mountain slope and repair damaged forests after the karhutla to prevent landslides and flash floods in the rainy season.
 "After the karhutla and drought yesterday, the hills became fragile and difficult to absorb water. Once it rains heavily in late October, the risk of landslides and flash floods from the mountain is very high," said Iwan Suryawan in Bandung, Saturday (31/10/2026).
 Iwan reminded that the threat of disasters in the highlands should not be taken lightly by all parties. "Based on the recapitulation of BPBD West Java data as of October 2026, more than 488 natural disaster incidents in West Java have been recorded, dominated by landslides and flash floods in mountainous areas," he continued.
 He proposed a re-mapping of red zones in highlands such as Bogor, Sukabumi, Cianjur, West Bandung, Garut, to Tasikmalaya. "The slopes of the bare or burned mountains must be immediately replanted with strong-rooted trees so that the soil structure is locked and is not easily eroded during heavy rains," said Iwan.
 Officers in the field are also asked to immediately check the physical condition of the cliffs, mountain waterways, and mud retaining embankments so that they are not clogged with residual fire materials. "For quick handling in the field, we encourage the optimal use of the Unexpected Expenditure budget until the end of the year," he explained.
 According to him, the emergency fund must be prioritized for the mitigation of hydrometeorological disasters, including alerting heavy equipment at landslide-prone points. "In addition to heavy equipment, the equally important thing is to train residents of the slopes through the Tangguh Bencana Village to be able to detect the early movement of the ground," added the legislator.
 He also encouraged assistance for sloping land farmers to apply safe cultivation techniques that are safe from the threat of soil erosion. "The provincial government must ensure that the landslide hazard marker or Early Warning System works well, considering that there are around 150,000 people living in the red zone of the central mountains," said Iwan.
 Iwan emphasized that the West Java DPRD is ready to support budget oversight so that all of these hydrometeorological disaster mitigation programs run smoothly in the field. "People who live near our slopes are urged to always be alert and immediately report if they see cracks in the ground, trees leaning, or the river water suddenly murky," said Iwan.
